items.stem: What is meant by a solute?
items.answer: The substance that dissolves in a solution, usually present in smaller amount
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A solute – the substance that dissolves in a solution, usually present in smaller amount.

items.stem: In soda water, the solvent is:
items.markingKey: (a) Water is the solvent in which carbon dioxide dissolves.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Water dissolves many substances.
Reason (R): Water is called a universal solvent.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (b) Both true; R is a name given because of A, not the explanation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Sort these into substances insoluble in water and soluble in water: sawdust, chalk powder, sugar, alum, common salt.
items.answer: Insoluble in water: chalk powder, sawdust. Soluble in water: alum, common salt, sugar.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Insoluble in water: chalk powder, sawdust. Soluble in water: alum, common salt, sugar.

items.stem: Sort these into substances insoluble in water and soluble in water: sand, chalk powder, copper sulphate, common salt, sugar.
items.answer: Insoluble in water: chalk powder, sand. Soluble in water: common salt, copper sulphate, sugar.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): Insoluble in water: chalk powder, sand. Soluble in water: common salt, copper sulphate, sugar.

items.stem: Iodine does not dissolve easily in water, yet a doctor's "tincture of iodine" is a clear solution. Explain, and say what this tells us about solvents.
items.answer: Tincture of iodine is iodine dissolved in alcohol; different solvents dissolve different solutes, so water is not a solvent for everything.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: alcohol solvent. 1 mark: conclusion.

items.stem: Which of these substances is soluble in water?
items.markingKey: (b) Baking soda is soluble in water. The others: sand – insoluble in water; iron filings – insoluble in water; sawdust – insoluble in water.

items.stem: Which of these substances is insoluble in water?
items.markingKey: (b) Chalk powder is insoluble in water. The others: alum – soluble in water; common salt – soluble in water; glucose – soluble in water.

items.stem: Water is called a universal solvent because:
items.answer: it dissolves a large number of substances
items.markingKey: (b) it dissolves a large number of substances.
options: it dissolves a large number of substances

items.stem: Which of these substances is insoluble in water?
items.markingKey: (a) Wax is insoluble in water. The others: copper sulphate – soluble in water; sugar – soluble in water; glucose – soluble in water.

items.stem: Which of these substances is soluble in water?
items.markingKey: (d) Glucose is soluble in water. The others: sawdust – insoluble in water; sand – insoluble in water; chalk powder – insoluble in water.

items.stem: A saturated solution of sugar at 30 °C is heated to 60 °C. It becomes:
items.markingKey: (d) unsaturated.

items.stem: A saturated solution of potassium nitrate in 100 g of water is made at 60 °C (solubility 106 g) and cooled to 40 °C (solubility 62 g). What mass of crystals separates out? Name the process.
items.markingKey: (b) 106 − 62 = 44 g comes out as crystals on cooling (crystallisation).

items.stem: Why does a cold bottle of soda water fizz more when it warms up after opening?
items.answer: Carbon dioxide is less soluble in warm water, so it escapes as bubbles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: less soluble when warm. 1 mark: CO₂ escapes.

items.stem: The solubility of potassium chloride in water at 60 °C is 46 g per 100 g of water. What mass of potassium chloride is needed to make a saturated solution in 50 g of water at 60 °C?
The solubility of common salt in water at 40 °C is 36 g per 100 g of water. What mass of common salt is needed to make a saturated solution in 100 g of water at 40 °C?

Read: The solubility of potassium chloride (g per 100 g of water) is: 20 °C – 35 g; 40 °C – 40 g; 60 °C – 46 g.
(i) How does solubility change with temperature? (ii) What mass of potassium chloride will make a saturated solution in 100 g of water at 40 °C? (iii) A saturated solution in 100 g of water at 60 °C is cooled to 20 °C. What mass of crystals forms? (iv) Name this method of getting crystals.
items.answer: (i) It increases with temperature. (ii) 40 g. (iii) 46 − 35 = 11 g. (iv) Crystallisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: Students added sugar spoon by spoon to 100 mL of water at room temperature, stirring each time. After 18 spoons, sugar settled at the bottom. On heating, it dissolved, and more sugar could be added.
(i) What kind of solution was formed after 18 spoons? (ii) What did heating show? (iii) What will happen on cooling the hot solution? (iv) Name one use of this process.
items.answer: (i) A saturated solution. (ii) Solubility of sugar increases with temperature. (iii) Excess sugar will separate out as crystals. (iv) Making sugar crystals/purifying substances (crystallisation).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: A saturated solution of potassium nitrate in 100 g of water is made at 60 °C (solubility 106 g) and cooled to 20 °C (solubility 32 g). What mass of crystals separates out? Name the process.
items.markingKey: (d) 106 − 32 = 74 g comes out as crystals on cooling (crystallisation).

items.stem: The solubility of common salt in water at 60 °C is 37 g per 100 g of water. What mass of common salt is needed to make a saturated solution in 200 g of water at 60 °C?

Assertion (A): A saturated solution can dissolve more solute at the same temperature.
Reason (R): A saturated solution holds the maximum solute at that temperature.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define a concentrated solution.
items.answer: A solution that contains a large amount of solute in a given amount of solvent
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A concentrated solution – a solution that contains a large amount of solute in a given amount of solvent.

items.stem: Gauri dissolves 12 g of salt in 120 g of water. Calculate the concentration of the solution as mass by mass percentage.
items.markingKey: (d) Mass of solution = 12 + 120 = 132 g; concentration = 12 ÷ 132 × 100 = 9.09%.

items.stem: Why is it more useful to state the concentration of a solution as a percentage rather than as "strong" or "weak"?
items.answer: A percentage gives an exact, comparable amount of solute; "strong" or "weak" is vague and differs from person to person.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: exact. 1 mark: comparable.

items.stem: Saanvi dissolves 30 g of salt in 45 g of water. Calculate the concentration of the solution as mass by mass percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass of solution = 30 + 45 = 75 g; concentration = 30 ÷ 75 × 100 = 40%.

items.stem: How much sugar and how much water are needed to make 100 g of a 5% (mass by mass) sugar solution?
Harpreet dissolves 12 g of sugar in 88 g of water. Karthik dissolves 40 g of sugar in 160 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Harpreet: 12/100 × 100 = 12%; Karthik: 40/200 × 100 = 20%. Karthik's is more concentrated.

items.stem: How much sugar and how much water are needed to make 150 g of a 15% (mass by mass) sugar solution?
Fatima dissolves 10 g of sugar in 90 g of water. Kunal dissolves 40 g of sugar in 160 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Fatima: 10/100 × 100 = 10%; Kunal: 40/200 × 100 = 20%. Kunal's is more concentrated.

items.stem: 20 g of glucose is dissolved in water to make 500 mL of solution. What is the concentration as mass by volume percentage?
items.markingKey: Concentration = 20 ÷ 500 × 100 = 4% (g per 100 mL).

items.stem: 25 g of glucose is dissolved in water to make 200 mL of solution. What is the concentration as mass by volume percentage?
items.markingKey: Concentration = 25 ÷ 200 × 100 = 12.5% (g per 100 mL).

items.stem: 20 g of glucose is dissolved in water to make 250 mL of solution. What is the concentration as mass by volume percentage?
items.markingKey: Concentration = 20 ÷ 250 × 100 = 8% (g per 100 mL).

items.stem:
Read: A health worker in a village prepares ORS by dissolving 2.6 g of salt and 13.5 g of glucose in clean water to make 1 litre (1000 mL) of solution.
(i) Name the solvent and the solutes. (ii) Find the concentration of glucose as mass by volume %. (iii) Is the solution homogeneous? (iv) Why must boiled and cooled water be used?
items.answer: (i) Solvent: water; solutes: salt and glucose. (ii) 13.5 ÷ 1000 × 100 = 1.35%. (iii) Yes. (iv) To kill germs so the patient is not infected again.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Rohan dissolves 5 g of salt in 90 g of water. Calculate the concentration of the solution as mass by mass percentage.
items.markingKey: (d) Mass of solution = 5 + 90 = 95 g; concentration = 5 ÷ 95 × 100 = 5.26%.

items.stem: Which of the following is an object that sinks in water?
items.markingKey: (a) A coin is an object that sinks in water. The others: coconut oil drops – an object that floats in water; a cork – an object that floats in water; ice – an object that floats in water.

items.stem: The SI unit of density is:
items.markingKey: (b) kg/m³.

items.stem: Why is it easier to float in the sea than in a river?
items.answer: Sea water is denser because of dissolved salts, so it pushes up with a greater buoyant force.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: denser. 1 mark: greater buoyant force.

items.stem: A glass marble has a mass of 52 g and a volume of 20 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 52 ÷ 20 = 2.6 g/cm³; more than water, so it sinks.

items.stem: The density of milk is 1.03 g/mL. What is the mass of 500 mL of milk?
items.markingKey: Mass = density × volume = 1.03 × 500 = 515 g.

items.stem: A lactometer shows that a milk sample has a density of 1.01 g/mL, while pure milk is about 1.03 g/mL. What can you conclude? Explain.
items.answer: The milk has probably been diluted with water (density 1.00 g/mL), lowering its density.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: adulterated with water. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Ice sinks in water.
Reason (R): Ice is less dense than water.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A cork has a mass of 5 g and a volume of 20 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25 g/cm³; less than water, so it floats.

items.stem: Oil floats on water. This shows that oil:
items.answer: has a lower density than water
items.markingKey: (d) has a lower density than water.
options: has a lower density than water

items.stem: A plastic toy has a mass of 48 g and a volume of 40 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 48 ÷ 40 = 1.2 g/cm³; more than water, so it sinks.

items.stem: Arrange honey, water and coconut oil in layers in a glass, from bottom to top, and explain your order using densities (honey 1.4, water 1.0, coconut oil 0.92 g/mL).
items.answer: Bottom: honey; middle: water; top: coconut oil. Denser liquids sink below less dense ones.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: order. 1 mark: reason.

items.stem: A plastic toy has a mass of 120 g and a volume of 100 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2 g/cm³; more than water, so it sinks.

items.stem: Nandini dissolves 15 g of sugar in 85 g of water. Ananya dissolves 25 g of sugar in 225 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Nandini: 15/100 × 100 = 15%; Ananya: 25/250 × 100 = 10%. Nandini's is more concentrated.

items.stem: Om dissolves 15 g of sugar in 85 g of water. Saanvi dissolves 18 g of sugar in 132 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Om: 15/100 × 100 = 15%; Saanvi: 18/150 × 100 = 12%. Om's is more concentrated.

items.stem: A cork has a mass of 25 g and a volume of 100 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 g/cm³; less than water, so it floats.

items.stem: Dev dissolves 20 g of sugar in 180 g of water. Rohan dissolves 40 g of sugar in 160 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Dev: 20/200 × 100 = 10%; Rohan: 40/200 × 100 = 20%. Rohan's is more concentrated.

items.stem: The solubility of potassium chloride in water at 40 °C is 40 g per 100 g of water. What mass of potassium chloride is needed to make a saturated solution in 100 g of water at 40 °C?

items.markingKey: (d) Water is the solvent in which sugar dissolves.

items.stem: Saanvi dissolves 5 g of salt in 175 g of water. Calculate the concentration of the solution as mass by mass percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass of solution = 5 + 175 = 180 g; concentration = 5 ÷ 180 × 100 = 2.78%.

items.stem: Why does powdered sugar dissolve faster than a sugar cube?
items.answer: Powder has a larger surface area in contact with water, so particles mix with water faster.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: surface area. 1 mark: faster mixing.

items.stem: Sneha dissolves 20 g of sugar in 180 g of water. Kunal dissolves 30 g of sugar in 170 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Sneha: 20/200 × 100 = 10%; Kunal: 30/200 × 100 = 15%. Kunal's is more concentrated.

items.stem:
Read: The solubility of potassium nitrate (g per 100 g of water) is: 20 °C – 32 g; 40 °C – 62 g; 60 °C – 106 g.

items.answer: (i) It increases with temperature. (ii) 62 g. (iii) 106 − 32 = 74 g. (iv) Crystallisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Aquatic animals breathe oxygen that is:
items.markingKey: (d) dissolved in water.

items.stem: A block of wood has a mass of 30 g and a volume of 50 cm³. Find its density. Will it float or sink in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 30 ÷ 50 = 0.6 g/cm³; less than water, so it floats.

items.stem: How much sugar and how much water are needed to make 500 g of a 2% (mass by mass) sugar solution?
Define crystallisation.
items.answer: The process of getting pure crystals of a substance by cooling a hot saturated solution
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Crystallisation – the process of getting pure crystals of a substance by cooling a hot saturated solution.

items.answer: its hollow shape makes its average density less than that of water

items.markingKey: (d) Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve in 100 g of a solvent at a given temperature.

items.markingKey: Density = mass ÷ volume = 24 ÷ 20 = 1.2 g/cm³; more than water, so it sinks.

items.stem: Sahil dissolves 30 g of salt in 175 g of water. Calculate the concentration of the solution as mass by mass percentage.
items.markingKey: Mass of solution = 30 + 175 = 205 g; concentration = 30 ÷ 205 × 100 = 14.6%.

items.stem: Why is water important for living organisms as a solvent?
items.answer: Nutrients, gases and wastes dissolve in water and are carried in blood and plant sap; reactions in cells take place in water.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: transport of dissolved substances. 1 mark: reactions.

items.stem: Diya dissolves 10 g of sugar in 90 g of water. Saanvi dissolves 18 g of sugar in 132 g of water. Whose solution is more concentrated? Show your working.
items.markingKey: Diya: 10/100 × 100 = 10%; Saanvi: 18/150 × 100 = 12%. Saanvi's is more concentrated.
